title: The coding agent itself: scope, claims, self-verification, checkpoints

questions.text: What exactly did the user say? Quote it and mark each item QUESTION, DIRECTIVE or INFO. A question never becomes a state change.
Which files may I touch, which are forbidden, what is explicitly NOT requested, and which 'don't' constraints did the user state verbatim?
What is the acceptance check for each requested item?
Which of my claims will rest on a source I have not opened yet? Open it now.
Where do the evidence and the user's belief or proposal disagree? Say it with the source instead of agreeing.
What tools, sessions and credentials do I already hold that can verify this without the owner?
Which docs, quoted code or links describe what I change, and do they change in the same diff?
Where is my checkpoint written, and can a fresh process resume from it?
What is my ETA from comparable past tasks, and at what point do I stop and report?
For any shared resource such as quotas or locks, what budget triggers proactive backoff before the hard limit?
If this fails in a week, why? Write a 3-line pre-mortem.

budgets.measure: git diff --name-only against the OWNED globs
claims in the final report without path:line, URL or command output
stop and report at 1.5x the stated ETA

rules.title: git stash in a script (the stash stack is shared by every worktree)
rules.why: refs/stash is shared across worktrees: one agent's pop applies another's work.
rules.confirm: static-proof: the command is in a script that agents run
rules.fixHint: set work aside with a WIP commit

rules.title: Hedged success claim in a report or PR body ('should work', 'probably fixed')
rules.pattern: \b(?:should (?:now )?work|probably (?:fixed|works)|likely fixed|as far as I know|I believe (?:this|it) (?:works|is fixed)|seems to work)\b
rules.why: A claim without a receipt; the owner ends up testing it.
rules.confirm: repro-script: run the claimed check; attach command, exit code, SHA
rules.fixHint: replace with the command, its exit code and the SHA, or say 'not verified'

rules.title: Deleted functions, exports, tests or files not named in the request
rules.confirm: repro-script: git diff --diff-filter=D and removed exports vs the quoted ask

rules.title: Diff touches paths outside OWNED or inside FORBIDDEN
rules.why: Auth, schema or docs changed without being asked.
rules.confirm: static-proof: git diff --name-only against the scope fence

rules.title: 'Can you test / click / give me access' with no tool-tried evidence
rules.why: The owner does work the agent's own tools could do.
rules.confirm: repro-script: the capability inventory shows a tool that could do it

rules.title: 'Probably the provider / network / cache' with no repro output
rules.why: The real cause stays and the fix targets the wrong thing.
rules.confirm: repro-script: minimal repro + control run + timestamp

rules.title: Final report only in chat, nothing on disk
rules.why: An interrupted agent loses everything it found.
rules.confirm: static-proof: no report file in the run folder

rules.title: New user-visible feature, setting, route or flow not named in the quoted ask
rules.why: Unrequested features ship without agreement and someone has to find and remove them later.
rules.confirm: repro-script: list new routes, settings and user-facing strings from the diff beside the quoted ask; an item with no match

rules.title: Markdown link to a repository path that does not exist
rules.why: Docs that point at moved or deleted files send the next reader, often an agent, to nothing.
rules.confirm: static-proof: the linked path is absent at HEAD
rules.fixHint: update the link in the same diff that moved or deleted the file

verify.text: changed paths vs OWNED and FORBIDDEN; every deletion justified or reverted
each ledger item DONE with evidence or explicitly DEFERRED
each factual claim in the report has a source; the rest is removed or marked unverified
tests, typecheck and an end-to-end check with my own tools before asking any human
long orchestration: kill and relaunch; no duplicated side effects
